data_boundary: calibrated-v2 development captures only for captured-audio noise/dropout selection; no calibrated-v2 held-out capture entered selection
prior_art_boundary: Prior Cora M9 and Corollary evidence identify representation normalization and ambient-noise sensitivity as active risks; geometry remains fixed until a stable condition gate exists.

noise_audit.perturbation: deterministic white sensor noise at a token-relative RMS SNR
noise_audit.grammar_only_result: Predictive improvement remained positive at 10 dB but at least one state disappeared; 8 dB collapsed predictive advantage.
noise_audit.same_condition_calibration_result: With the same noise present in all four unlabeled calibration observations and grammar tokens, every leave-one-development-trial-out fold retained four states and beat its best causal baseline at 10 dB.

dropout_audit.selection_reason: 10 percent was the strongest tested condition for which every leave-one-development-trial-out fold retained all four states; at 15 percent one fold lost a state.

speaker_shift_audit.perturbation: synthetic source F0 profile change with unchanged formant targets
speaker_shift_audit.boundary: F0 variation is a controlled synthetic-speaker proxy, not evidence of transfer across recorded human speakers.

selected_condition_matrix.combined_shift: All held-out vowel trials use the unseen 200 Hz F0; noise and dropout conditions add one perturbation each.

design_gate: Advance only because the selected noise, dropout, and prospective F0 conditions preserve four states and at least 0.20 predictive improvement in their respective development/synthetic audits.
claim_boundary: This is design evidence only. A real pass would support calibrated adaptation under three controlled perturbation conditions, not recorded-speaker or natural-stream robustness.
